tables.title: Test-Set Performance
notes: Trained on 399 cases, tested on 133 held-out cases (25%, seed 123).
The no-information rate is the accuracy of always predicting the largest class.

tables.title: SHAP Summary
notes: SHAP values are on the probability scale for the class 'Yes'.
Estimated by Monte Carlo sampling (30 permutations) for 133 test cases.

assumptions.message: Accuracy is 17.0 points higher on the training data than on the test data; the model may be overfitted.

interpretation.text: A random forest predicting diabetes from 7 predictors classified 79.7% of 133 held-out cases correctly (95% CI [71.9, 86.2]; κ = 0.52), compared with 69.9% for always predicting the largest class. The AUC was 0.846. The most important predictor was glucose.

title: Random Forest
code:
library(ggnext)
# Random forest (classification): diabetes ~ pregnancies + glucose + blood_pressure + skin_fold + bmi + pedigree + age
predictors <- c("pregnancies", "glucose", "blood_pressure", "skin_fold", "bmi", "pedigree", "age")
d <- data[complete.cases(data[, c("diabetes", predictors)]), c("diabetes", predictors), drop = FALSE]
d$diabetes <- droplevels(factor(d$diabetes))
d$diabetes <- droplevels(d$diabetes)
# Hold out 25% of the cases to test the model
set.seed(123)
test_rows <- sample(nrow(d), round(0.25 * nrow(d)))
train <- d[-test_rows, , drop = FALSE]
test <- d[test_rows, , drop = FALSE]
fit <- ranger::ranger(diabetes ~ ., data = train, num.trees = 500, probability = TRUE, importance = "permutation", seed = 123)
predict_fn <- function(newdata) predict(fit, data = newdata)$predictions
oob_error <- fit$prediction.error
# Performance on the held-out test set
classes <- levels(train$diabetes)
prob <- predict_fn(test)
pred <- factor(colnames(prob)[apply(prob, 1, which.max)], levels = classes)
confusion <- table(Predicted = pred, Actual = test$diabetes)
n_test <- sum(confusion)
accuracy <- c(sum(diag(confusion)) / n_test, binom.test(sum(diag(confusion)), n_test)$conf.int)
chance <- sum(rowSums(confusion) * colSums(confusion)) / n_test^2
kappa <- (accuracy[1] - chance) / (1 - chance)
no_information_rate <- max(colSums(confusion)) / n_test
by_class <- data.frame(class = classes, sensitivity = diag(confusion) / colSums(confusion),
                       specificity = (n_test - rowSums(confusion) - colSums(confusion) + diag(confusion)) / (n_test - colSums(confusion)),
                       precision = diag(confusion) / rowSums(confusion))
by_class$f1 <- 2 * by_class$precision * by_class$sensitivity / (by_class$precision + by_class$sensitivity)
train_accuracy <- mean(colnames(prob)[apply(predict_fn(train), 1, which.max)] == train$diabetes)
roc_obj <- pROC::roc(test$diabetes, prob[, classes[2]], levels = classes, direction = "<", quiet = TRUE)
auc <- c(pROC::auc(roc_obj), pROC::ci.auc(roc_obj)[c(1, 3)])
importance <- sort(fit$variable.importance, decreasing = TRUE)   # permutation importance on out-of-bag cases
# SHAP values by Monte Carlo sampling (Strumbelj & Kononenko, 2014): how much each predictor
# moves each test-set prediction away from the average prediction
shap_fn <- function(newdata) predict_fn(newdata)[, classes[2]]   # probability of the second class
explain <- test[seq_len(min(nrow(test), 200)), predictors, drop = FALSE]
n_sim <- 30
shap <- matrix(0, nrow(explain), length(predictors), dimnames = list(NULL, predictors))
set.seed(123)
for (i in seq_len(n_sim)) {
  current <- train[sample(nrow(train), nrow(explain), replace = TRUE), predictors, drop = FALSE]   # background cases
  before <- shap_fn(current)
  for (v in sample(predictors)) {
    current[[v]] <- explain[[v]]
    after <- shap_fn(current)
    shap[, v] <- shap[, v] + (after - before) / n_sim
    before <- after
  }
}
shap_importance <- sort(colMeans(abs(shap)), decreasing = TRUE)
importance_df <- data.frame(variable = names(importance), importance = as.numeric(importance))[seq_len(min(length(importance), 20)), ]
importance_df$variable <- factor(importance_df$variable, levels = rev(importance_df$variable))
# Names are drawn inside the panel, left of the data (ggnext clips long axis labels)
label_pad <- min(0.5, (max(nchar(as.character(importance_df$variable))) * 7 + 12) / 500)
importance_df$label_x <- min(0, importance_df$importance) - (max(importance_df$importance) - min(0, importance_df$importance)) * label_pad / (1 - label_pad)
p_importance <- ggnext(importance_df, aes(importance, variable)) +
  geom_importance() +
  geom_text(aes(x = label_x, y = variable, label = variable), anchor = "start") +
  labs(title = "Variable importance", x = "Importance") +
  theme(axis_title_y = FALSE, axis_text_y = FALSE, base = theme_modern())
roc_df <- data.frame(truth = as.integer(test$diabetes == classes[2]), score = prob[, classes[2]])
p_performance <- ggnext(roc_df, aes(truth = truth, score = score)) +
  geom_roc() +
  labs(title = "ROC curve (test set)", x = "1 − Specificity", y = "Sensitivity") +
  theme_modern()
shap_long <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(shap_importance), function(v) {
  x <- as.numeric(explain[[v]])
  data.frame(feature = v, shap = shap[, v], value = (x - min(x)) / max(diff(range(x)), 1e-9))   # value scaled 0 to 1
}))
shap_long$feature <- factor(shap_long$feature, levels = rev(names(shap_importance)))
shap_labels <- data.frame(feature = factor(levels(shap_long$feature), levels = levels(shap_long$feature)))
# Names are drawn inside the panel, left of the data (ggnext clips long axis labels)
label_pad <- min(0.5, (max(nchar(as.character(shap_labels$feature))) * 7 + 12) / 430)
shap_labels$label_x <- min(shap_long$shap) - (max(shap_long$shap) - min(shap_long$shap)) * label_pad / (1 - label_pad)
p_shap <- ggnext(shap_long, aes(shap, feature)) +
  geom_shap(aes(color = value)) +
  geom_vline(0, dash = "4 4") +
  geom_text(aes(x = label_x, y = feature, label = feature), data = shap_labels, anchor = "start") +
  labs(title = "SHAP values (test set)", x = "SHAP value", color = "Predictor value") +
  theme(axis_title_y = FALSE, axis_text_y = FALSE, base = theme_modern())
